qualifiers.snapshot: An asterisk marks effectiveness by creature type as determined by die roll; consult item description.
Double asterisk: DM misleads the possessor regarding harmful nature; poison has a dash in the sale-value column.
Gold-piece sale values are usual sums paid; sold items use selling price for experience award.
DMG p.122 ring ‡ marks powerful rings that may have limited charges at DM discretion; (M) means magic-user only.
DMG p.122 rods, staves and wands values assume full charges; (C), (F), (M), (T) designate cleric, fighter, magic-user and thief, (any) any class unless otherwise prohibited.
DMG p.122 bracers of defense: 3,000 gp per armor class above 10; example AC 6 is worth 12,000 gp if sold.
Miscellaneous magic table 2, DMG p.123: * per plus of protection; ** add 100% for each additional feature; *** if reverse effect, 50,000 gp sale value.
DMG p.123 table 3: * per hit die of figurine; ** double for a bronze horn, triple for an iron horn; *** per stone; **** per level of instrument for bards.
DMG p.123 table 4: * per hit die of each missile; ** per special bead; *** per pot of pigments; **** per level of spell.
DMG p.124 special artifact table: these items bring no experience points; printed Orb of the Dragonkind value is “10–80,000”, preserved exactly rather than silently expanded.
